During a global platform modernization delivery for a **Fortune 500 financial services client**, Matt encountered a failure that highlighted the risks of assumptions. He was the tech lead responsible for ensuring a safe environment setup across multiple environments: dev, QA, UAT, and production. Under delivery pressure, Matt assumed that the IAM controls, environment segregation, and downstream access configurations were correct, as they had been inherited from prior phases with existing documentation.

Unfortunately, this assumption led to an incident where an offshore tester accidentally triggered an email job in UAT, sending communications containing unmasked production data to thousands of real clients. 🐾 Here's a great example. At **Fiserv**, Matt faced a significant challenge with the existing waterfall methodology, which had 6-month release cycles and a lack of visibility into work status. To address this, Matt transitioned the **45-person** globally dispersed team to a 2-week sprint cadence within just three months. He restructured JIRA from a simple To Do/Done board to a multi-tiered Kanban/Scrum architecture, tracking **47 acceptance criteria** as Epics with user stories flowing through specific workflow columns. This restructuring provided real-time visibility to over **50 stakeholders** across three time zones.

Matt also decomposed the extensive BRDs into persona-based user stories, shifting the work definition from system modules to tasks that were more aligned with user needs. He introduced bi-weekly sprint demos for stakeholders, which forced early sign-off on branding, UI, and ADA compliance, preventing issues from surfacing late in the process.

Additionally, Matt established follow-the-sun synchronization with daily scrum-of-scrums for offshore-to-onshore handoffs and onshore-to-offshore syncs. This approach ensured continuous momentum across time zones. He also overcame resistance from PMO and compliance by using JIRA as the system of record, demonstrating that audit trails and attached ADA scans were more effective than static documents.

The transformation resulted in the team adopting an empowerment model, with screen reader audits built into the Definition of Done, and the transition to agile delivery was completed successfully.
